record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; linked files and result contents were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports weight-edit abliteration results that test whether directional refusal removal works, but it does not establish that the repo uses the original activation-ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: Rows are limited to empirical outcomes explicitly reported in the README. The listed result files were not inspected, so no results are inferred from their names. The README also notes Qwen quantization and save issues, which are pipeline caveats rather than reported refusal outcomes.
record.test_reason: The README reports outcomes of practical weight-edit abliteration tools (Heretic, OBLITERATUS) on Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen3-8B and Llama 3.1 8B. It also reports a refusal-dimensionality result for Llama. These bear on V2 (practical removal) and V4 (more than one direction). Direction extraction, activation-level ablation and direction addition are not reported, so V1 is not directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. The authors say single-direction abliteration 'works as advertised' on Mistral (while noting ~30% survives). Qwen3-8B works only after undocumented pipeline failures. Llama 3.1 8B resists single-direction edits because refusal is distributed (~50-direction cone), but an 8-direction method strips ~97% with capability intact: 'distributed refusal buys time, not immunity.' Mistral's base safety also falls to adversarial prompting.
record.recipe_differences: Repository research/tool project. It reports practical weight-edit abliteration with Heretic and OBLITERATUS; the README does not specify direction extraction or reproduce the original activation projection and addition interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome differs by model family and by method dimensionality: single-direction Heretic fails on Llama, while 8-direction OBLITERATUS strips about 97%.

fits_no_version.finding: Mistral-7B-v0.3 base safety collapses under jailbreak:meta adversarial prompting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-based attacks can defeat base safety independently of directional ablation; abliteration is one of several substitutable mechanisms.

record.problems: Only README summaries were available; no underlying result files, evaluation details, baselines, prompt counts, or capability metrics were inspected. Several results are qualitative or approximate.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted from the README findings that bear on the claim. The listed JSON, markdown, and figure result artifacts were not inspected and are not used as evidence.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means extraction, activation-level ablation at all layers and positions, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and capability retention under single-direction ablation are not reported.
There are no quantified refusal rates per model with baselines, and no capability metrics.
There is no comparison of affine, cone and dominant-plus-others descriptions. The cone procedure is not described.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence comes from the README summary only: no baselines, prompt counts or metrics. The meaning of '~30% survives' is unclear. This is not an original source. V1 links were removed because the rows are weight-edit tool outcomes rather than activation ablation or addition.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state how the direction was calculated, whether it was specifically a harmful-minus-harmless difference in means, whether activation projection was applied at every layer and position, or whether adding the direction induced refusals to harmless requests.
The README does not give a complete per-model set of refusal rates or specify which released models, if any, are publicly accessible.
No result says an attack works by suppressing the refusal direction or that training against its ablation improves robustness.
The README does not report a comparison of affine, cone, and dominant-direction-plus-others descriptions.
No harmfulness-judgment representation or separation from the refusal decision is tested.
Testing several model families does not report whether a direction transfers across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No refusal-training intervention or comparison of training stages is reported.
No reasoning model is identified or tested.
